reason: Under the transfer lens the idea passes two checks and fails three. PASSES: (a) nodes are untouched and N_pred does not include edges, so there is no node-count-multiplier artefact; (b) the gain does not depend on trusting in-sample edge_prob (the rule is geometry; the side rule only uses 'unscored', a kNN property). FAILS: (1) The safety margin is measured on in-sample positions. The detector was trained on these 199 videos, so TP-fork node positions are optimistic. TP max mid 3.76 vs threshold 4.0 is a 0.24 um margin (0.15 of a z voxel). 7 of the 11 removed FP have a z offset of 3.2-5.0 um, so the rule is mainly a z-offset rule, and z is the worst-localised axis on unseen data. Adding extra per-node out-of-sample error (sd z 0.4/0.6/0.8/1.0 um, xy 0.15-0.4; scratchpad/fm_transfer3.py) gives P(TP fork lost) at 4.0 um of 1.4/2.8/4.2/6.5%. The research's 2.4-3.8% fit assumed no in-sample shift. (2) The effective sample is one embryo. 10 of 11 removed FP come from 6bba (30% of its FP forks). 44b6 loses only 1 of 10 (10%), and all 44b6 TP mids are <= 2.51. With the public TP 19 / FP 13 and +0.0069 J per FP vs -0.0189 J per TP: at a 44b6-like FP rate the public EV is +0.0009 at zero TP loss, -0.0001 at 2.8% and -0.0006 at 4.2%. Only a 6bba-like embryo gives a robust +0.0004..+0.0027. The sign on private embryos is therefore not established. The thresholds were also read off all 199 videos, so no clean held-out check exists. (3) Population mismatch on the ship base. The audit covered exp39 safe-division forks, which the symmetry and divergence gates had already pre-selected to have a small mid. exp48/exp51 also carries DaughterNet divinsert forks (mid <= 6.5, no symmetry gate), whose TP mid distribution is unmeasured, and 21% of GT divisions have mid >= 4 um. The refined change applies forkmid to 'every 2-child fork', which contradicts the research's own pitfall 3. It could remove divinsert TP forks and undo part of probe 28's +0.001 public gain. 4 of the 11 removed FP also have an unscored (prob 0) ILP-side edge, so they may overlap with the edge-filter base; the marginal count on the bundle base is unmeasured. The local gain is real but tiny (+0.0007). Its transfer sign at 4.0 um is uncertain, not established.
fix_if_any: (1) Apply the rule only to safe-division edges (NaN-prob, safe_division==1); exclude div_inserted forks, or first measure divinsert TP mids on an exp48 replay graph and exempt them. (2) Use 4.5 um, not 4.0. In the same noise simulation, P(TP lost) at 4.5 um is 0.2/0.6/1.3/2.6%, it still removes 6 local FP (11-15% on a 44b6-like embryo, 18-22% on 6bba), and the public EV stays >= about +0.0005 even for a 44b6-like embryo at z-noise sd 0.8. A z-robust alternative is an xy-only offset >= 4.0 um (P(TP lost) <= 0.9%, but only 4-5 FP). (3) Re-derive the threshold on the coord-head (float) graph, and require the margin over the TP max to be >= 0.7 um (about 0.5 z voxel), not 0.25. (4) Measure the marginal FP removed on the actual bundle base (exp48 + edge filter), because 4 of the 11 targets have prob-0 ILP-side edges. (5) Ship only inside a bundle, and pre-register that it is dropped if any TP fork is lost on either embryo.
realistic_public_gain: About +0.0000 to +0.0010 for the 4.0 um rule on all forks (negative tail about -0.0006 if the public/private embryos look like 44b6 and z localisation degrades out of sample). About +0.0005 to +0.0009 for the repaired 4.5 um, safe-division-only variant. Not observable on the LB by itself.
